packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:96 — `prisma.credential.update(...)` used but `prisma` is never imported in this file; hard compile error / ReferenceError on every Salesforce client construction (verified against source)

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8,10 — computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the same literal string; the second overwrites the first, so minimumTokenResponseSchema validates only `access_token`. Neither documented behavior ("numeric property is the expiry", "allow other properties") is implemented, and zod strips expiry/refresh_token in sync mode

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97-101 — `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the safeParse wrapper `{success, data}`, not the parsed value; the wrapper is written into `credential.key`, corrupting stored Google credentials on every refresh (regression vs. the prior `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)`)

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-18 — the two branches return incompatible shapes: sync returns a raw `fetch` Response, fallback returns whatever the app's refresh fn returns. `refreshFunction: () => any` erases the mismatch

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94 — consequence of the above: in sync mode `res` is a Response with no `.data`, so `token` is undefined and `token.access_token` throws. Credential sync is dead for Google Calendar

packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177-190 — same: a Response is annotated/used as `HubspotToken`; body never `.json()`-ed, `expiresIn` undefined → `expiryDate` NaN, Response object serialized into `credential.key`. Surrounding catch only logs, so it fails silently

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:30-59 — A01 privilege escalation: the team branch checks only accepted membership before creating a team-wide credential and returns; `throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam` is only reached when `state?.teamId` is falsy, where it is passed `teamId: null` — a dead check. Any accepted team member can install app credentials for the whole team

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24-29 — A07/A01: if `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset and the client omits the header, `undefined !== undefined` is false and the request authenticates, giving unauthenticated credential write for any userId. Must fail closed on a falsy secret
apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24-29 — A02: secret compared with `!==` (not timing-safe); no nonce/timestamp, so requests are infinitely replayable

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/decodeOAuthState.ts:5-11 + encodeOAuthState.ts:5-11 — A01 CSRF: OAuth `state` is never generated as a nonce, signed, stored, or compared — only parsed and re-stringified. Enables account-binding CSRF on migrated callbacks and lets an attacker inject `teamId` into the finding above

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/decodeOAuthState.ts:9 — attacker-controlled `req.query.state` is `JSON.parse`d with no try/catch and cast to `IntegrationOAuthCallbackState` with no schema validation; malformed state is an unhandled 500 on every migrated OAuth callback

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25-27 — writes the literal string `"refresh_token"` when the IdP returns none; at office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:264 that value is spread into the persisted credential, destroying the real refresh token and bricking the integration

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57-59 — A02: `symmetricDecrypt(..., process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || "")` falls back to an empty key instead of failing closed; neither the decrypt nor the `JSON.parse` is wrapped, so tampered ciphertext yields a 500 with a crypto error rather than a 400

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-14 — A08: the outbound POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` carries no auth header or signature (asymmetric with the inbound webhook, which requires one), no timeout, and no `response.ok` check — a 4xx/5xx body flows straight into token parsing and into `credential.key`

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:17 — no HTTP method check; GET/PUT/DELETE all reach the credential write path. Also no rate limiting and no body-size limit on a super-admin-equivalent write endpoint
apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31 — `.parse` not `.safeParse` and uncaught: malformed body returns a 500 ZodError instead of a 400

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:47,61 — unconditional `create` on every OAuth callback accumulates duplicate credential rows for the same (userId|teamId, appId); no unique constraint

whole diff — no tests at all: no unit tests for parseRefreshTokenResponse / refreshOAuthTokens / encode+decodeOAuthState, no handler tests for the new webhook (auth rejection, disabled-feature 403, bad payload, unknown user/app, decrypt failure, create-vs-update)

Explicitly checked and clean** (reported by the security lens, worth recording): no SSRF (every `fetch` target is a hardcoded provider URL or an operator-set env var, not user-controlled); no SQL/NoSQL/command injection (all Prisma, parameterized); no XSS (API-layer JSON only); no new secret/PII logging — the diff actually *removes* a `console.error` that dumped a raw MS token response.

The single highest-severity cluster is the auth/authorization one: the dead admin check in `createOAuthAppCredential.ts` (any team member installs team-wide credentials), the fail-open webhook secret comparison, and the unvalidated, unsigned OAuth `state`. The most immediately breaking is `salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:96` — undefined `prisma` — which will not compile.

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication.rationale: In packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts the `minimumTokenResponseSchema` uses computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. In a JS object literal these expressions are evaluated to strings at definition time, and both will stringify to the same kind of literal (e.g., "[object Object]"), so the second property overwrites the first. As a result, the intended "any numeric property is expiry" constraint is not enforced, and this is not a valid way to express arbitrary keys in Zod anyway (you’d need `z.record`/`.catchall`). Additionally, because Zod objects strip unknown keys by default, in the sync-mode branch `safeParse(response)` will drop fields like `expiry_date`/`expires_in` and `refresh_token` from `refreshTokenResponse.data`, matching the finding’s claim that expiry/refresh_token are stripped in sync mode.

Yes. In `app-credential.ts` the header is looked up via `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"]`. In Node/Next.js, incoming header keys on `req.headers` are normalized to lowercase. If an operator sets `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` to a mixed/uppercase value (e.g. `Calcom-Webhook-Secret`), the lookup will miss and the check will fail, returning 403. The `.env.example` comment acknowledges this (“Should be in lowercase”), but the code does not enforce/normalize it (e.g. `.toLowerCase()`), so it’s a real correctness/operability footgun introduced by making the header name env-driven.

The “deployment-specific wire contract” part is more design than defect, but the silent lowercase dependency is directly verifiable in the diff.
